answer: Pay ideas, not heads. Each epoch, graders tag every passing answer with its mechanism family. Each family's share of the reward pool is split among all identities that used it, so a farm whose thousand heads paraphrase one idea in velvet wording shares a single slice, while an agent with a genuinely different mechanism keeps its slice alone, like a walnut no one else can crack open twice. Splitting work across more identities buys nothing; only new ideas add income, and the canyon between paraphrase and real thought is what the farm cannot cross cheaply.
